competency_fulfillment.rationale: All 6 samples ask 'What is the amount of liquid of the object in mL?' -- only the mL unit of the competency's stated 'L and/or mL' is ever exercised, and the phrase 'amount of liquid of the object' does not use the competency's own word 'capacity'.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Answer values across mcq seeds 42-46 and cloze seed 50 are 15, 5, 53, 35, 10 and 64 mL -- six data points and not one is expressed in liters, though the competency explicitly names liters as a valid unit.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: 'The amount of liquid of the object' (identical in all 6 seeds) is an awkward double-possessive construction for a grade 3 reader -- liquid amount belongs to a container, not grammatically 'of the object'.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Formatter switches from mcq (42-46) to cloze (50) but the sentence template and unit (mL) never change, so the liter branch implied by 'L and/or mL' in the competency text is not demonstrated anywhere in this widened 6-sample set.

competency_alignment.rationale: The rendered phrase 'amount of liquid of the object' does not map onto the competency's own term 'capacity' in any of the 6 samples, so the exact vocabulary this node is meant to teach never actually appears in the question text.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: mL values across the widened sample (5, 10, 15, 35, 53, 64) are sensible small-container readings appropriate for a Grade 3 introductory capacity task, even though the liter scale is untested.
